entries.title: February 1981 Nellis procedures
facts: Cover is dated February 1981.
Pages 7-8 publish 22 ATC points and 10 navaids.
LOTUS ONE, PLAZA 1 and FLEX procedures appear on pages 10-12.
limits: Unknown coordinate datum; do not silently merge with modern fixes.
PLAZA STAR includes a DME arc; reconstructed route needs separate geometry review.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: 1981 tanker tracks and entry references
facts: Page 13 lists AR624, AR625 HI/LO, AR635, AR641A, AR230V and AR231V.
limits: AR641A entry is N/A.
Schematic racetracks do not establish complete vertices, leg lengths or turns.
Mixed level notation is retained without inventing pressure bases.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: 2014 Elgin, Sally and weather recall
facts: Elgin is marked VMC only, 13K-FL230.
Simultaneous North/South War procedures generally close Sally and open Elgin.
Recall gates specify Caliente north of N37-40 and Coyote north of N37-48 at/above FL310.
limits: Missing exact polygon boundary vertices.
FL230 and FL310 must stay flight levels.
MOPAR is a western recovery point, not an Elgin vertex.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Normandy: group movement and squadron arrival
facts: Wing heritage says parts of the 36th Group began moving to Brucheville on 4 July 1944.
Official 53 FS station date is circa 7 July 1944; official 23 FS date is 3 August 1944.
limits: Group movement is not proof of arrival of every squadron.
Current June 21 Normandy preset already discloses some airfield substitutions; this would refine them, not newly discover all of them.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Bitburg and Spangdahlem aircraft transitions
facts: F-100 on 13 March 1956; first F-105s on 13 May 1961; F-4C/D arrivals began 20 March 1966.
All three flying squadrons completed F-4E conversion by 30 September 1973.
F-15A/B arrivals on 27 April 1977; GULLY JUMP moved flying operations to Spangdahlem July-November 1968.
limits: F-15A/B is not the DCS F-15C.
36 TFW / Wing is not the 36 TFS at Osan.
A 2017 heritage repaint pictured in the pamphlet is not a contemporary 1973 livery photograph.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Aircraft markings, unit identity and deployments
facts: The downloaded lineage sheets are compilations and may lose qualifiers.
70 FS operated F-4s at Moody in 1975-1987, followed by F-16s; the 1989 Ramstein deployment is outside its F-4 period.
limits: A squadron name or modern museum repaint alone does not certify a DCS skin.
Do not overwrite measured parking directions using historical parking row labels.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Swift Move 1973: carrier alert in northern waters
facts: VF-14 describes Norwegian/North Sea operations, sometimes above the Arctic Circle, ending 8 October 1973.
Reported 92 sorties / 163 hours and 18 Soviet interceptions: 12 Tu-95 and 6 Tu-16.
limits: No exact patrol tracks or carrier coordinates.
VF-14 then used F-4B, not F-4E; carrier was JFK, CVA-67.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Mediterranean fleet alert, October-November 1973
facts: JFK assumed station south of Crete on 25 October 1973.
VF-14 maintained five-minute alert and intercepted Soviet An-12 / An-22 resupply transports.
All twelve F-4Bs were transferred in December during preparations for F-14A transition.
limits: Current filename says VFA-14; original 1973 designation is VF-14.
This does not establish an Israeli, Egyptian or Syrian air corridor, nor exact carrier station geometry.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Proven Force: Incirlik and the 1991 air order of battle
facts: GWAPS Volume V Table 6 lists airfields and aircraft by monthly snapshot.
Incirlik column for 1 February 1991 includes 4 F-4Es, 15 F-4Gs and 6 RF-4Cs.
limits: A monthly snapshot is not proof of unit identity, every intervening day or sortie routes.
1991 falls outside current Cold War 1965-1985 and modern 2000s+ presets.
Do not substitute F-4E for F-4G without disclosure or infer livery from aircraft totals.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: OIF 2003: the air campaign and changing airspace
facts: USCENTAF By the Numbers is dated 30 April 2003, covering 0300Z 19 March to 0259Z 18 April.
Reports approximately 1,800 control measures in database, about 1,200 managed daily, about 12 ACO changes daily.
limits: The report says initial best-available figures, not final analytical findings.
The totals do not supply corridor coordinates or individual validity windows.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: VF-11: F-14B training and workups in 2003
facts: VF-11 reported 11 F-14B aircraft, tail AG, assigned to USS George Washington CVN-73.
April, July and August-September 2003 entries document Fallon training; autumn documents ship workups.
limits: Do not label the entire 2003 report an OIF combat deployment.
Fallon training cannot be silently relocated to Nellis as an exact recreation.
Original designation VF-11, not current VFA-11.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Moody 1979: a scheduled F-5 aggressor visit
facts: 347 TFW NIP 22 describes a planned 65 FWS visit, 25 June-6 July 1979, with 108 aggressor sorties across three squadrons and academics on 22 June.
limits: This planning document does not prove all scheduled sorties took place.
Moody is outside supported maps; any playable relocation is an adaptation.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: 1980 F-4E weapons and identification references
facts: Pave Spike instructor handout marked revised June 1980.
Dive Toss NIP 30 dated June 1980.
AN/APX-80A NIP 28 dated March 1980.
limits: No promise of unsupported DCS avionics or automatic coaching.
Dive Toss material and four 70 TFS pamphlets already underpin existing courses; do not duplicate them as newly invented syllabi.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Analog and digital F-4E configurations
facts: March 1978 TAC Attack describes ARN-101 procurement for block 48 and later aircraft and anticipated 1979 introduction.
The 3 TFS New Guy Part 2 material describes ARN-101 DMAS.
limits: A 1978 forecast is not proof of fielding dates or retrofit completion for every squadron.
Do not treat every Cold War F-4E as identical or infer a pamphlet date from the filename.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Osan 1978: two-seat briefing and evaluation
facts: 36 TFS Mission Procedures dated 14 September 1978 include Osan forecasts, GCI, threat of the day and crew planning.
2 October 1978 Top Gun program relies on gun-camera film, including 24-fps scoring criteria.
limits: 36 TFS Osan is not 36 TFW Bitburg.
Do not promise automatic DCS scoring of historical film-frame gun solutions.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Red Flag 1978: coordination and debrief lessons
facts: March 1978 Red Flag Mistakes article by a 70 TFS / 347 TFW pilot discusses interservice visual-signal misunderstandings and recce/strike formation coordination.
limits: Narrative lesson is not a complete exercise SPINS document or universal regulation.
Do not claim automated evaluation of every behavior described.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Southeast Asia: weather, guided bombs and changing ROE
facts: Guided Bomb Operations in SEA: The Weather Dimension covers 1 February-31 December 1972; report dated 1 October 1973.
Explains target acquisition, cloud/haze limitations and specific supported delivery exceptions.
Separate ROE report covers November 1969-September 1972, dated 1 March 1973.
limits: Vietnam/Laos geography is not faithfully recreated by drawing its historical boundaries on Syria or Sinai.
Period experimental techniques and Paveway I configurations must not be assumed to exist in current DCS modules.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.

entries.title: Afghan air forces and civil wars, 1989-2001
facts: Lukas Müller’s 2020 history focuses on Afghan air forces, rather than detailing foreign air operations.
Its chapter periods distinguish the Najibullah government (1989-1992), factional wars (1992-1996), the Taliban’s northern conquest (1996-1998), and later advances and fall (1999-2001).
These periods differ from the product’s post-2003 War on Terror setting.
limits: Secondary historical interpretation; unit and aircraft claims require case-by-case corroboration.
No corridor coordinates or operational airspace validity established.
entries.simulation_support: Reference reading; does not add a flown route, aircraft system or scoring trigger.
